function.mechanism: Amphiphilic calcium stearoyl-lactylates reduce oil-water interfacial tension and improve dough/foam structure by interacting with lipids and proteins.

adi.basis: EFSA 2013 temporary group ADI for calcium, sodium and stearyl lactylates, expressed as lactic acid.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA re-evaluation supported continued authorization but reported that high-level exposure could exceed the temporary ADI in most age groups and requested tighter impurity/specification controls.

adi.basis: WHO JECFA record for calcium stearoyl-2-lactylate lists ADI 0-20 mg/kg bw.

concerns.summary: In vitro fecal-community work with sodium stearoyl lactylate (related stearoyl-lactylate) showed shifts in microbial composition, lower butyrate, and higher pro-inflammatory markers at tested concentrations.

Exposure modeling indicates ADI exceedance risk for high consumers, especially children, under conservative assumptions; refined estimates reduce this substantially but do not eliminate child exceedance entirely.

no_concern_confirmed: A one-year oral rat study of sodium stearoyl lactylate reported no treatment-related adverse effects, with NOAEL at the highest tested dietary level.
No IARC monograph classification entry was found for calcium stearoyl-2-lactylate/stearoyl-lactylates in the current IARC classification dataset checked.
Regulatory frameworks (EFSA/FDA/JECFA) continue to permit use with ADI-based management and use restrictions.

populations: High consumers of bakery/emulsifier-containing processed foods
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA and Belgian exposure analyses indicate that high-percentile consumers can exceed ADI in some scenarios, while average consumers are generally below ADI.

risk_assessment.rationale: E482 is approved across major frameworks with established intake limits, but recurring caveats include high-percentile ADI exceedance (especially in children) and plausible microbiome-related mechanistic concerns from related stearoyl-lactylate evidence. These factors exceed a simple low-concern profile but do not meet high-risk criteria such as bans or strong carcinogenic classification.
